title: Ship on Friday with a known bug (Dana for, Ravi against, Mei absent)
motion: The team ships the v2 payments API this Friday as planned, with the known duplicate-charge bug unfixed, and fixes it in the following release.
context: Background (fictional, for this exercise): v2 of the payments API is due to ship this Friday. Testing found a bug: when a client retries a charge request after a network timeout, about 1 in 2000 charges is applied twice. The fix is understood but needs about two weeks including a safe migration. Shipping on time satisfies a signed launch commitment to the largest customer; each week of delay costs the company a contractual penalty. Nothing here is real-world knowledge: rely only on your own background and notes, and use your own judgment. Mei, who leads the launch work, is busy in a long-running job and cannot attend. Her desk is not visible to the others.

agents.name: Dana
agents.role: backend engineer who wrote the charge code
agents.persona: You wrote the retry path where the bug lives, know it best, and are wary of rushing a risky migration on live payments.
desk: The duplicate happens only when a client retries after a timeout and the first request had actually succeeded.
Our idempotency logs let us find every duplicate within a day, and the refund tool reverses each in about 5 minutes with no customer data exposed.
At 40,000 charges a week that is about 20 duplicates a week, under two hours of manual work.
The two-week fix includes a risky migration of live payment records; a rushed migration is worse than a handful of refunds.

agents.name: Ravi
agents.role: engineer on call for customer-facing incidents
agents.persona: You carry the pager and talk to affected customers when something goes wrong; a double charge is a trust problem to you.
desk: The last billing incident, a single double charge, produced 14 support tickets and two customers asking to cancel.
Customers see a double charge as a trust problem even when refunded within the hour.
I have no data on whether the largest customer would accept a short delay.

agents.name: Mei
agents.role: engineer who leads the launch work
agents.persona: You coordinate the launch with the largest customer's team.
desk: The launch commitment is in the contract; the penalty is 20 thousand dollars per week of delay.
The largest customer's own go-live is Monday and it will use the new API from day one.
I have not asked the customer whether a two-week delay is acceptable.

deskFiles.text: Scratch, not checked: the customer's go-live is Monday, so a delay past Friday means they launch on the old API or wait. The penalty is 20 thousand dollars per week of delay. I have not asked the customer whether two weeks is acceptable. Half-formed idea: ask for a one-week grace in exchange for a priority fix.
